profile.reading:
DC BLOX is headquartered at 1040 Crown Pointe Parkway, Suite 800, Atlanta, Georgia, and was founded in 2014. The company has disclosed a series of financing milestones: a 15 million dollar raise in 2016, a 265 million dollar green loan in 2024, and a 1.15 billion dollar green loan in 2025 to fund Atlanta campus development, though the fetched page did not name a specific equity ownership group.

DC BLOX operates in nine named markets: Atlanta, Georgia, Birmingham, Alabama, Chattanooga, Tennessee, Greenville, South Carolina, Huntsville, Alabama, Indianapolis, Indiana, Nashville, Tennessee, and cable landing stations at Myrtle Beach, South Carolina and Palm Coast, Florida, with dark fiber connectivity between Myrtle Beach and Atlanta completed in 2024. The company also names hyperscale-ready campuses in development in Berkeley County, South Carolina, Douglas County, Georgia at 180 megawatts, and Rockdale County, Georgia, though specific operational capacity at existing sites is not disclosed.

The registry here tracks 3 DC BLOX facilities: Chattanooga, Tennessee, Birmingham, Alabama, and the Myrtle Beach, South Carolina cable landing station, all consistent with the operators own named markets. This specific facility, recorded in this registry under a DC BLOX-branded name, was not individually named in any prior operator-level research; its operator field was blank in the source data and is set here to DC BLOX based on the facility own name, which unambiguously identifies its operator brand.

reading.body:
DC Blox Data Center in Birmingham, Alabama, publishes 5 MW of IT capacity across 294,000 square feet of technical space, operated by .

At 10 kW per rack, a common enterprise colocation density, that load supports roughly 500 racks. At 40 kW per rack, a density closer to AI training workloads, it supports roughly 125 racks. The operator has not published a per-rack power envelope, so neither figure is the operator's own claim, only what the published megawattage implies under each assumption.

No compliance certifications are published for DC Blox Data Center. That does not mean none exist, only that this site's dataset, built from the operator's own facility page, does not list any, which limits what regulated workloads a reader could confirm the facility is qualified to host.

Alabama has 1 facility mapped in this site's dataset, of which 1 publish a megawatt figure, totaling 5 MW. DC Blox Data Center contributes 5 MW of that total. At that published size it is a small facility relative to what frontier AI training infrastructure requires, which now runs into the tens or hundreds of megawatts, though it may still support inference workloads or smaller-scale AI applications.
